chunks: From Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created a group of creatures whom He kept away from trials; He created them in well-being, gave them life in well-being, caused them to die in well-being, and entered them into Paradise in well-being.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be kept away from trials by Allah?
ai.summary: In the context of *Kitab al-Mumin*, this hadith highlights the divine grace reserved for the faithful, emphasizing that their entire lifecycle—from creation to entry into Paradise—is marked by 'afiyah' (comprehensive well-being and safety from harm). This concept underscores the Shia belief in Allah's protective care for believers, distinguishing their spiritual and physical journey from those subjected to trials. The emphasis on continuous well-being reflects the idea that true faith brings inner peace and divine protection throughout all stages of existence.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 83. It has been reported that Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said: I heard him (al-Sadiq (a.s)) saying:

Allah has (some) creatures that He keeps away from trials. He creates them in well-being, gives them life in well-being, grasps their souls in well-being and causes them to enter Paradise in well-being.
